audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Overheat as Rumble's damage state — 'an overheated Flamespitter walks you down', 'Build heat to overheat his next Flamespitter so his sustained AP burns through your short trades'. That is backwards.
audit.why: Junkyard Titan gives two separate states. At 50% Heat he enters Danger Zone, where his basic abilities gain bonus effects — that is the empowered Flamespitter. At 100% Heat he starts Overheating: he gains attack speed and bonus damage on basic attacks but is unable to cast spells for a few seconds. A player who reads this entry will back off exactly when Rumble is at his most castable and step in when his abilities are actually empowered.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone (50% heat) is the empowered Flamespitter; Overheat (100%) locks his casts and turns him into an auto-attacker. Fight him into Overheat, not away from it.

audit.why: The ability is The Equalizer. The packet flagged this as a probable wrong name and the kit confirms it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer nominates Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining cooldown to track and step up on.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a flat 6s at every rank — shorter than Mel's Q at any rank and barely half her snare. It is up for essentially every trade, so 'trade just after he burns it' is not a window at all. Electro Harpoon is worse: 0.5s between casts with two charges held. The only real clock in this lane is the heat bar.
audit.corrected: Track heat, not Scrap Shield. Commit as he crosses into Overheat, when his casts are locked.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow.
audit.why: It also reduces Magic Resist, and Rumble carries two charges. Against an AP champion that shred is the reason his follow-up Flamespitter hurts more than the numbers on the tooltip suggest — reflecting the harpoon with Rebuttal denies the slow and the shred in one.
audit.corrected: Name the MR reduction and the two-charge stock alongside the slow.

edits.before: Rumble's biggest threat: an overheated Flamespitter walks you down through your kite if his E harpoon slow lands first — respect the heat bar.
edits.after: Rumble's biggest threat: a Danger Zone Flamespitter walks you down through your kite if Electro Harpoon's slow lands first — watch the heat bar.

edits.before: Land E harpoon to slow you, then overheat Flamespitter and walk you down out of root range
edits.after: Land Electro Harpoon to slow you and shred your MR, then walk you down with Flamespitter

edits.before: Build heat to overheat his next Flamespitter so his sustained AP burns through your short trades
edits.after: Sit above 50% heat so every Danger Zone Flamespitter burns harder through your short trades

edits.before: Drop Equalizer across your kite path so you can't poke from max range safely
edits.after: Drop The Equalizer across your kite path so you can't poke from max range safely

edits.before: Use Rebuttal's wall to eat his E harpoon projectile and deny the slow that sets up his DPS
edits.after: Reflect Electro Harpoon with Rebuttal to deny both the slow and the magic resist shred

edits.before: He gets W shield and move speed online to answer your trades, so your level-3 spike that crushes immobile melee is blunted into even here.
edits.after: Scrap Shield is a flat 6s, so it answers nearly every poke — the level-3 spike that crushes immobile melee flattens to even here.

edits.before: Your Q ranks build Overwhelm, but his overheated Flamespitter and E slow trade back — it stays a coinflip of who lands their setup first.
edits.after: Your Q ranks build Overwhelm, but a Danger Zone Flamespitter and Electro Harpoon's slow trade back — it stays a coinflip on setup.

edits.before: This is a genuine coinflip, not a free lane. Your Q ranks and Overwhelm stacks build pressure, but every time Rumble overheats Flamespitter he out-DPSes your short trades, and his E slow strips the kite you live on. Use Rebuttal to eat the harpoon projectile — no slow means no overheat trade lands. At 6 your Golden Eclipse detonates your stacks from range, but don't walk into his Equalizer to do it; bait the heat bar to overheat into a cooldown, then commit when his Flamespitter is mute.
edits.after: This is a genuine coinflip, not a free lane. Your Q ranks and Overwhelm stacks build pressure, but a Danger Zone Flamespitter out-DPSes your short trades, and Electro Harpoon's slow plus MR shred strips the kite you live on. Reflect that harpoon with Rebuttal — no slow, no trade. At 6 your Golden Eclipse detonates your stacks from range, but don't walk into The Equalizer to do it; bait him past 100% heat, where Overheating locks his casts, then commit while he can only auto.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Check it before every step-up. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Rumble Scrap Shield: a flat 6s, so it covers nearly every poke — the heat bar, not the shield, is the clock. Commit as he crosses 100% and Overheating locks his casts. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Scrap Shield before stepping up.
edits.after: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — Scrap Shield is 6s, so read the heat bar instead and step up as he crosses into Overheat.

edits.before: Track Rumble’s Scrap Shield: Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Rumble’s heat bar ahead of Scrap Shield: at 100% he Overheats and his casts lock, and that is your step-up window.

edits.before: Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Shield and speed on a flat 6s cooldown — the heat bar, not the shield, tells you when to step in.

edits.before: Reflect Scrap Shield back the moment he commits
edits.after: Reflect Electro Harpoon the moment he throws it

notes: The packet's suspectName 'Solar Snare's' is a false positive — Mel's real E name with a possessive. 'Drop Equalizer' was a genuine name error and is corrected. Six games behind the 50% figure, so the level chart was left as-is.
